items.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998
items.q: I played with Tito Puente, Tito Rodriguez, Sonny Dunham, a bunch of bands.

ctx.x: As a free lance musician, what’s the best way for you to — I’m talking in general — get your reputation out there?

I was lucky I had a reputation before I got to New York. I had a reputation from the Sauter-Finegan Orchestra from the ‘50s. I was in New York in ‘48 but that was sporadically. I didn’t settle in New York until ‘53, and that was with the Sauter-Finegan Orchestra. And my name had gotten around from playing with that band, although I had played with other bands, well I played with Ray McKinley’s band after that. I played with Tito Puente, Tito Rodriguez, Sonny Dunham, a bunch of bands. Some — I only remember one,…
Was the recording scene pretty healthy in the ‘50s once you got out and started to get into studio work?
